subject: Inference migration: clarifying deployment mode and migration constraints
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@medora.com>, Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@medora.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Inference migration: initial post-call recap and ask

Thanks again for your time earlier, Elena and Rajesh — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same signal on constraints and preferred path.

Call summary (very high level)
- Current state: Medora running a self-hosted GPU cluster (internal name: infer-ops) for most production traffic plus an older hosted endpoint for non-PII workloads.
- Primary drivers: reduce perf variance, lower token cost, and meet PHI/data residency/compliance requirements for certain customers.
- Migration interest: evaluate Hosted API for quick POC, Dedicated capacity for steady-state predictable throughput, or Private VPC/on-prem for full compliance.

Key constraints you flagged
- PHI scope: some request routing must stay inside a VPC (US-only).
- Encryption: KMS-backed keys mandatory for model artifacts and KV cache.
- Cutover: procurement window target is end of Q3; production cutover target is Nov 2027.
- Lift constraints: existing infer-ops processes include custom latency-sensitive batching and a homegrown KV layer.

Requests / next steps
1) Please confirm whether the infer-ops cluster is behind a NAT with fixed egress IPs (we need allowlisting) — Rajesh to confirm. (attachment: medora-inference-matrix.pdf we discussed)
2) We'll send a short cost/latency sketch for three paths: Hosted POC, Dedicated reservation, and Private VPC (on-prem variant). Karthik to own.
3) Security artifacts: you've asked for SOC 2 + P48 equivalence. Monica attaching the checklist and we can follow with the formal questionnaire.
4) Technical sync: propose a 30-minute engineering call next week to get RPS/peak tokens and KV cache TTLs.

Attachments: medora-inference-matrix.pdf, medora-security-p48.pdf

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks, Hannah — quick clarifications from our side:
- infer-ops is an on-prem cluster (NVIDIA A100s) behind a corporate NAT. We do have a small pool of static egress IPs but need to confirm the exact ones.
- Our initial migration scope is: move non-PII traffic to Hosted for validation; PII/PHI traffic must either remain on-prem or move to a Private VPC with keys we control.
- Cost is important but compliance + deterministic latency for some customers is a hard constraint.

I can bring our infra lead (Elena) into the technical call; she can share the cluster telemetry and batch behavior.

-Rajesh

Appreciate the context, Rajesh. A few technical bullets that will help us size options and give you the right tradeoffs: 
- Target QPS/RPS in steady state and 95th-percentile latency SLOs (token-level info helps us choose quantization/batching profiles).
- Typical prompt + response token counts (median / 95th) and whether you use long-context KV caching per session.
- Peak burst profile (daily or monthly spikes) and acceptable warm-up time for cold KV caches.
- Are you able to share a sanitized sample trace or the batch-size distribution? That materially changes the Dedicated sizing.

Quick note on tradeoffs (short):
- Hosted API: fastest POC (hours), lower engineering lift, but will not satisfy PHI/full VPC isolation without Private add-on. Good for traffic validation.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools under your tenancy (predictable throughput + cost). Supports custom kernels/quantization and better SLA guarantees.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full data residency and KMS control; higher ops cadence and procurement overhead. Can be configured with HSM/KMS and network isolation.

Proposed next step: 30 minute technical sync next Tue/Wed. I'll prepare three rough cost scenarios (hosted POC, 3-month Dedicated pilot, Private VPC baseline) in advance.

-- Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving & Performance
Redwood Inference
